assumptions: Tỷ VND. Toy ghi expected malpractice obligation khi đủ recognition; insurer recovery ghi riêng khi accepted, không bù obligation. Legal defense expense đã phát sinh separate.

evidence.text: [Claim] Bệnh viện có claim xác nhận phải bồi thường, settlement estimate ba mức 20 (20%), 40 (50%), 70 (30%). Toy probability-weighted provision, no discount.
[Recovery] Bảo hiểm chấp thuận recovery cố định 25 tỷ, chưa thu. Cash advance bồi thường cho claimant 8 tỷ đã trả, dùng provision.
[Legal] Chi phí luật sư 3 tỷ đã trả, không nằm settlement estimate.
[P&L] Operating profit trước malpractice và legal cost 100 tỷ. No opening provision/recovery.
[Memo] Director muốn ghi net liability bằng provision trừ insurer 25, và dùng payout 8 làm total claim expense.

qas.question: Find expected malpractice settlement before payment.
Find unpaid claimant provision after cash advance.
Find recognized insurer recovery asset at reporting date.
Calculate net P&L charge from claim, recovery and legal expense.
Find hospital operating result after the recognized incident items.
Why does the accepted insurance recovery not reduce gross claimant obligation?
qas.answer: The hospital owes claimant separately and has a distinct insurer recovery right; the toy requires gross presentation.

qas.question: Is the 8b payment an additional expense beyond the recognized provision?
qas.answer: No. It settles part of the provision already recorded.

qas.question: Can the actual final court award be known exactly?
qas.answer: No. The scenario distribution is an estimate, not a final court judgment.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Toy thay đổi residual value và remaining life áp prospective từ đầu kỳ hiện tại; không restate prior depreciation. No tax.

evidence.text: [Fleet] Original cost 300 tỷ, accumulated depreciation 120 tỷ đầu năm, carrying 180. Previously remaining life 6 years, residual 30.
[Revision] Engineering approved remaining life 4 years and residual 20 as of Jan1 due to heavier usage. No impairment, purchases or disposals.
[Operations] Freight revenue 500, cash operating cost 390. No finance expense.
[Cash] All operating receipts/payments settled; opening cash 40; cash fleet maintenance capex 25 not yet ready for use, separate from revised fleet.
[Draft] Controller proposes recalculating all prior depreciation based on new residual and life.

qas.question: Find annual depreciation under the old remaining estimates.
Find current depreciation using revised estimates prospectively.
Find incremental current depreciation versus old estimate.
Find carrying amount of the revised existing fleet at year end.
Find operating profit after revised depreciation.
Why not rewrite prior depreciation under the toy estimate-change policy?
qas.answer: The new information changes future useful life and residual estimates; apply prospectively, not as an error correction.

qas.question: Does incremental depreciation 15 cause a corresponding current cash outflow?
qas.answer: No. Depreciation is noncash; maintenance capex is a separate cash item.

qas.question: Can actual resale proceeds of the fleet be assured at 20?
qas.answer: No. Residual value is an estimate, not a binding sale.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Toy network component abandoned and removed, no salvage. Existing dismantling provision used for cash costs; additional estimate recognized expense only, not capitalized because component no future benefits.

evidence.text: [Network] Old equipment carrying 90 tỷ, abandoned permanently at year-end. No sale proceeds. New equipment not yet installed.
[Provision] Opening dismantling obligation 20 tỷ, cash removal cost 16 tỷ paid. Updated remaining removal estimate 10 tỷ, no discount.
[Policy] Additional provision needed after settlement expensed, not capitalized; old equipment derecognized.
[P&L] Operating profit trước abandonment/removal adjustments 200 tỷ. No tax.
[Memo] CTO claims all removal cash 16 and total new estimate 10 must be added to asset writeoff as current expense.

qas.question: Find equipment abandonment loss.
Find dismantling provision immediately after the cash removal payment.
Find additional provision required to reach revised remaining estimate.
Find total current abandonment-related P&L charge.
Find operating profit after current abandonment charges.
Why is 16 of cash removal not a second expense?
qas.answer: It settles a previously recognized dismantling obligation; only the incremental 6 is newly expensed.

qas.question: Why not capitalize revised removal estimate into the abandoned component?
qas.answer: The component has no future benefits and the toy explicitly expenses the revision.

qas.question: Can deployment cost for the replacement network be calculated?
qas.answer: No. No new equipment cost or installation data are provided.

assumptions: Triệu USD. Toy loyalty allocated consideration initially deferred; recognize cumulative redemption proportional to expected ultimate redemptions, with estimate revision catch-up. No expiry yet.

evidence.text: [Award cohort] 100m points issued, consideration allocated 20m. Initial expected ultimate redemption 80m points; 40m points already redeemed by prior year-end, revenue recognized 10m.
[Current] Additional 20m points redeemed, cumulative redeemed 60m. Approved expected ultimate redemption revised to 90m points.
[Policy] Cumulative revenue =20m × cumulative redeemed / expected ultimate redeemed. Revision applies cumulative catch-up; no cash receipt on redemption.
[Cost] Current reward delivery cost 3m; no other expense or changes in consideration.
[Draft] Manager recognizes 20m×20/80=5m current revenue using old expected redemption denominator.

qas.question: Find revised cumulative redemption proportion at reporting date.
Find cumulative loyalty revenue under the revised estimate.
Find current-period revenue after prior recognition of 10m.
Find remaining loyalty liability after catch-up.
Find current reward contribution after fulfillment cost.
Why does a higher expected ultimate redemption reduce recognized revenue for a fixed cumulative redeemed count?
qas.answer: The denominator rises, so a smaller fraction of allocated consideration has been earned under the toy model.

qas.question: Should current point redemptions be recorded as new customer cash receipts?
qas.answer: No. Consideration was allocated at issuance; redemption fulfills an existing obligation.

qas.question: Can remaining point redemptions be forecast precisely by month?
qas.answer: No. The ultimate estimate does not include monthly redemption timing.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Toy crop fair value less costs to sell measured at reporting; all planting costs expensed. No harvest yet; no tax.

evidence.text: [Opening] Growing crop carrying 50 tỷ. Year-end expected sale quantity 20 nghìn tấn, expected selling price 5 triệu/tấn, cost to sell .5 triệu/tấn.
[Revision] Earlier draft expected 25 nghìn tấn at same price/cost; approved agronomy forecast reduces quantity to 20. No harvest or physical sales yet.
[Cost] Planting and care cash costs this year 30 tỷ expensed, no purchases or other asset movement.
[Policy] Closing carrying uses expected sale value net cost to sell, changes recognized P&L. No discount or risk adjustment in toy.
[Memo] Manager treats expected crop sale value as actual cash revenue.

qas.question: Find approved closing crop value net of cost to sell.
Find draft crop valuation before yield revision.
Find reduction in estimated carrying value from draft.
Find current fair-value gain compared with opening carrying.
Find crop-related P&L after planting and care expense.
Why is the 90b closing value not actual sale proceeds?
qas.answer: The crop has not been harvested or sold; carrying value is based on estimated future selling economics.

qas.question: Should planting costs be added to the approved 90b carrying under the stated toy policy?
qas.answer: No. Costs are expensed and fair value is measured separately; adding them would double-count.

qas.question: Can exact final harvest profit be forecast?
qas.answer: No. Actual quantity, selling price and later cost may differ from estimates.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Toy campus asset impairment based on recoverable amount at change in use; no revaluation upward, no tax. Separate refurbishment capitalized only for qualifying improvements.

evidence.text: [Asset] Campus building carrying 500 tỷ trước impairment; enrollment decline leads to closing one wing. Approved recoverable amount 420 tỷ.
[Refurbishment] After impairment test, qualifying conversion of another wing costs 60 tỷ cash, ready only next year. Routine repair 10 tỷ expensed.
[Policy] Impairment first, then separate qualifying addition; no current depreciation on new conversion. Existing building depreciation already included in operating profit.
[P&L] Operating profit before impairment/repair 100 tỷ. No other capital movements or tax.
[Memo] Rector capitalizes both 60 and 10, argues new plan eliminates the need for impairment.

qas.question: Find the building impairment charge at the approved test date.
Find qualifying capital addition from conversion.
Find closing campus building carrying after impairment and addition.
Find current expense from impairment and routine repair.
Find operating surplus after the two current expense items.
Why cannot a new conversion plan automatically cancel the earlier impairment?
qas.answer: The approved recoverability test precedes the qualifying addition; the toy does not permit an unsupported reversal.

qas.question: Why is routine repair not part of the new conversion asset?
qas.answer: It is expressly nonqualifying maintenance, rather than a separate improvement.

qas.question: Can the next year's impairment test result be established?
qas.answer: No. Updated recoverability and utilization forecasts are missing.

assumptions: Triệu USD, million ore tonnes. Toy UOP depletion based on opening carrying less residual divided by opening recoverable reserve estimate; updated estimate applies prospectively at Jan1. No other additions or impairment.

evidence.text: [Mine asset] Opening carrying 240m, residual zero. Prior estimate remaining recoverable ore 60m tonnes.
[Revision] Approved exploration data revises remaining reserves at Jan1 to 48m tonnes. Actual ore extraction 6m tonnes in current year.
[Operations] Metal sales 180m, cash operating expense 120m. No other depreciation or tax.
[Policy] UOP expense=opening carrying×current extraction/revised opening reserves; no restatement of past depletion.
[Memo] Manager uses original 60m denominator because new reserve estimate is not cash spending.

qas.question: Find depletion expense under the old reserve estimate for current extraction.
Find depletion expense under the approved revised reserve estimate.
Find additional current depletion due to estimate revision.
Find closing mine asset carrying after depletion.
Find operating profit with revised UOP depletion.
Why does reduced reserve denominator increase depletion per tonne?
qas.answer: The same depreciable carrying is allocated across fewer recoverable tonnes.

qas.question: Should prior years' depletion be restated solely for the new reserve estimate?
qas.answer: No. The stipulated estimate revision is prospective.

qas.question: Can actual mine life be established from the remaining ore reserve alone?
qas.answer: No. Future extraction rates, mine plan and technical constraints are unknown.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Toy approved probable obligation measured at probability-weighted loss; legal costs separate. Uncertain unapproved regulator proposal not included unless already within scenarios. No tax.

evidence.text: [Incident] Utility environmental breach đã xác nhận; approved settlement scenarios 40 tỷ (25%), 80 tỷ (50%), 160 tỷ (25%). No discount.

[Legal] Opening provision 50 tỷ from prior period for same incident. Cash settlement advance 10 tỷ during current year, reduces obligation. Scenario values represent total remaining obligation at current reporting date AFTER this advance.
[Other] Legal fees 5 tỷ incurred and paid. Operating profit before current provision adjustment and legal fees 150 tỷ.
[Policy] Closing provision equals approved probability-weighted remaining loss. No insurer recovery.
[Memo] Regulator proposed 200 tỷ maximum in a press release, but no updated approved assessment; director claims 200 cash due immediately.

qas.question: Find probability-weighted remaining environmental obligation.
Find provision carrying after the 10b advance, before remeasurement.
Find incremental provision charge required at reporting date.
Find total current P&L charge including legal fees.
Find operating result after provision remeasurement and legal fees.
Why is subtracting the 10b advance again from the approved 90b estimate incorrect?
qas.answer: The scenario amounts are explicitly remaining obligations after the advance; another subtraction double-counts settlement.

qas.question: Does the press release prove a 200b current payable?
qas.answer: No. It is a proposal, not an approved updated obligation or payment schedule.

qas.question: Can actual settlement date be inferred from the probability distribution?
qas.answer: No. It specifies amounts and probabilities, not timing.
